purpose: CDK2 controlled failure diagnosis, scoped production repair, repeatability and artifact consistency evidence.

decision.recommendation: Use versioned NU6094 para-growth protocol with an appropriate transferred intermediate template and open 1H1S receptor; retain the original NU2058 N2 protocol separately.
decision.basis: The earlier miss was primarily incompatible receptor geometry plus insufficient local-search initialization, not absence of a larger neural model. Correct state identity and appropriate structural priors yielded repeatable selected-pose recovery with the existing CPU tools.
decision.scope: Curated structure-guided design and screening of a single para substituent on NU6094. This evidence does not validate arbitrary N2 growth, arbitrary proteins, binding affinity, potency, synthesis or clinical usefulness.
decision.retrospective_caveat: 1H1S was selected from the known NU6102 holo complex. NU6102 ligand coordinates were excluded from candidate placement, refinement and selection, but receptor choice is target-informed. This is not a fully prospective or blind test.
decision.unchanged_eligibility: PoseBusters dock geometry pass, nine-atom purine drift <=2 A, at least one Glu81/Leu83 hydrogen-bond interaction type. Asp86 contact is the objective, not a relaxed eligibility threshold.
decision.selection: Among eligible poses, prioritize Asp86-contact poses, then minimum Vina score; otherwise choose minimum-score eligible pose; otherwise retain the flagged minimum for inspection. Score alone is not the scientific objective.
decision.no_additional_ml_required: No new weights, paid cloud inference or custom forcefield were introduced to obtain these results.

implementation.state_identity_fix: Ordinary RDKit substructure queries did not require the aromatic nitrogen hydrogen count. The declared neutral9H scaffold now uses explicit [nH0+0]/[nH1+0] queries and records unique compatible tautomer normalization. No pH/tautomer ensemble is implied.
implementation.scope_rejections: NU2058 lacks the full NU6094 template; NU6086 is meta-substituted and outside declared para attachment. They remain diagnostic controls, not v2 production candidates.
implementation.source_provenance: NU6094 template uses 1H1Q ligand heavy atoms transformed by chain-A backbone alignment into ligand-free 1H1S. No NU6102 ligand SDF is bundled in the new live preparation.

critical_clash.description: Observed NU6102, transformed by receptor alignment into 1H1P, places sulfonamide N0.7423 A from Lys89CE. Local Vina refinement then displaces ligand2.556 A and loses Asp86/hinge contacts. In native1H1S, refinement moves it0.220 A and preserves the contacts.

diagnosis.flexibility_caveat: A single flexible Lys89 sidechain and bounded search did not recover the contact reproducibly. This does not rule out broader flexible docking or other models.

relaxed_parent_prior.finding: Locally relaxing NU2058 in open1H1S before growth still yielded zero eligible Asp86 cases in three32-attempt seeds.

nu6094_template_study.finding: The larger24-heavy-atom intermediate template gave repeated eligible recovery in open1H1S but not closed1H1Q across three seeds; no NU6102 ligand fit was used.

heldout_four_compound_benchmark.scope: Retrospective receptor-informed test in 1H1S: native NU6102 receptor, target ligand coordinates excluded from each placement input. Template sources explicitly exclude each held-out test compound. No property or contact thresholds tuned. P and Q use smaller/different priors than proposed NU6094-growth scope.
heldout_four_compound_benchmark.mapping_note: P=NU2058,Q=NU6094,R=NU6086,S=NU6102. Each compound placement excludes its own observed ligand coordinates; P uses common18 atoms from Q, Q uses P18, R/S use Q24. These are different priors, and P/R are not admitted by productionv2.
heldout_four_compound_benchmark.historical_label_correction: The local raw report originally mislabeled the Q scaffold as25 atoms in prose. It actually contains24 heavy atoms; all calculations used the correct molecule. Labels here and packaged runner are corrected.
heldout_four_compound_benchmark.coordinate_metric: Heavy-atom symmetry-aware RDKit CalcRMS against the observed ligand in the same receptor-aligned frame; no ligand fitting is performed during RMSD calculation.

limitations: Open receptor selection is retrospectively informed by the target compound holo structure.
A fixed known scaffold, one para attachment and selected neutral9H state constrain the tested chemical domain.
Rigid water-free receptor, computed hydrogen positions, local Vina scoring and limited conformer coverage remain approximations.
Any-pose recovery is distinct from selected-pose recovery; both are retained in benchmark evidence.
Generation is fixed-prior LibInvent sampling followed by screening, not online reinforcement-learning optimization.
No affinity, selectivity, ADMET, synthetic feasibility or experimental improvement claim follows from contact geometry.
Local raw-report paths are evidence locations for this validation session; compact case outcomes, hashes, configs and reproducible runners are versioned here.

Not benchmarked in this investigation. The positive scoped controls do not require such a swap, but do not establish superiority over those models. Benchmark one when expanding to unseen scaffolds/receptors or when this workflow fails representative controls.

model_tradeoff.reasoning: Vina optimize is a local refinement operation, not a guarantee of global recovery; accurate receptor and template priors can matter more than substituting a larger model. This conclusion is restricted to the measured fixed-scaffold task.
